# 05 — The creator flow, end to end

<!-- generated:status-banner -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

> **RC6 is LIVE AND OPEN ON THREE CHAINS.** RC6 is deployed and PUBLIC on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) and Robinhood Chain (4663): all three accept ordinary, permissionless creator launches. The factory is the same CREATE2 address on all three. RC6 is NOT deployed on BNB Smart Chain (56), which is deferred, and no date is set for it.
> Public creator launch is **open** on Ethereum (1), Base (8453), Robinhood Chain (4663) and **closed** on the other 1 configured chain.
> See [08 — Status and limitations](08-status.md).

<!-- /generated:status-banner -->

The flow is: **pick a chain → work in the studio → review → sign once.** One transaction does the
launch. There is no multi-step deployment you have to babysit, and no point at which a half-built
project exists on chain.

## Step 0 — Pick a chain

Four cards, one per configured chain. None is pre-selected, and the studio does not open until you
choose one.

<!-- generated:chains -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

| Chain | Chain ID | RC6 launch status | Default quote | Additional quote support | Explorer |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ethereum | 1 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | None. A non-WETH quote is refused by chain id, not by convention. | `etherscan.io` |
| Base | 8453 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | None. A non-WETH quote is refused by chain id, not by convention. | `basescan.org` |
| Robinhood Chain | 4663 | `DEPLOYED` · public launch open | WETH | Multi-quote. Any asset QuoteAssetRegistryV1 currently admits AND leaves enabled: the stablecoin, the Robinhood stock/ETF tokens and the ecosystem token. Governance admits; a bundle can only request. | `robinhoodchain.blockscout.com` |
| BNB Smart Chain | 56 | `PREPARED_NOT_DEPLOYED` · public launch closed | WBNB | None. WBNB is not WETH; never print "WETH" or "ETH" on this chain. | `bscscan.com` |

RC6 is live and open to ordinary creator launches on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) and Robinhood Chain (4663) -- one factory address, the same on all three, because the deployment is deterministic. BNB Smart Chain (56) is configured in the bundle format and the chain profiles and RC6 is not deployed on it; configured is not deployed, and no date is announced. The chains still differ in the quote leg -- Robinhood is the only multi-quote chain, and chain 56 settles in WBNB rather than WETH -- so read the row rather than assuming they match.

<!-- /generated:chains -->

Each card shows the chain id, the gas currency, the wrapped-native address, a live estimated launch
cost from a real block and gas-price read, the maximum script bytes for that chain, whether your
wallet is ready, and whether the platform is deployed there. Any fiat figure only appears if you
type a rate yourself — there is no price oracle inventing one for you.

Note the wrapped native is chain-local. On BNB Smart Chain it is WBNB and gas is paid in BNB;
"WETH" and "ETH" are the wrong words there.

**The chain is permanent.** Once a project is launched the cards go inert. There is no migration.

## Step 0.5 — What happens when you upload a `.relics` bundle

If you built a bundle with the creator kit, this is what the studio does with it. It is worth
reading because almost none of it is you doing anything.

1. **The raw bytes go to the server, not a client-parsed summary.** The browser inspects the file
   first as a convenience, and that run is never the authority: a patched client could skip it
   entirely. The same inspection code runs again server-side on the bytes you uploaded, and the
   studio refuses to populate a draft unless the **server** says the bundle is ready. A transport
   failure is treated as blocked, not as unknown-and-probably-fine.
2. **Every digest is recomputed, never trusted.** Per-file hashes, the bundle hash, the project
   config hash, the checksum manifest and the art binding are all re-derived from the bytes and
   compared against what the manifest declares. A file present but undeclared is a failure; a
   declared hash that does not match is a failure. So is a bundle whose representative outputs do
   not reproduce — "this file commits to X and its generator draws Y" is caught here rather than
   after launch.
3. **Your generator runs in a sandbox, on the server, and nowhere else.** It executes inside a
   worker thread and, within that, a VM realm with code generation disabled, a heap cap, a
   wall-clock timeout and a stripped global object: no `eval`, no `Function`, no `fetch`, no
   timers, no `Date`, no `crypto`, no `console`, no `Proxy`. `Math.random` is replaced with a
   function that throws and tells you to use the seeded PRNG instead. Only strings cross the
   boundary, and the render context is rebuilt inside the realm from JSON, so no host object is
   reachable. A sandbox failure is a refusal, not a pass. The browser runs none of it.
4. **The target chain is asked what it supports.** Whether the platform is deployed there, whether
   your art runtime and template are active *on chain*, whether your requested quote asset is
   admitted and still enabled, whether enforced creator earnings are offerable there, and what the
   script byte and gas budgets are. A client-supplied answer to any of these is deliberately
   ignored — a launch-gate row must not be movable by the thing it is gating.
5. **The launch configuration is derived, in one place.** The server builds the canonical
   `LaunchParams` from your draft, and derives rather than accepts the values that must not drift:
   `artScriptHash` is recomputed as `keccak256(artConfig)` against the exact bytes being submitted,
   and `metadataUriHash` is derived from the canonical metadata URI. Your art configuration bytes
   come out of the bundle and there is no encoder in the studio that could produce them by hand.
   Your launch-protection election is passed through with no fallback at all: an unset value is
   refused rather than resolved.
6. **Metadata is pinned and verified**, in the sequence in
   [13 — Collection metadata](13-metadata-and-contracturi.md), before anything is signed.
7. **Addresses are predicted, then the launch is simulated** — a real `eth_call` dry run against the
   deployed entrypoint. The transaction builder simulates again and returns a transaction only on
   success, so an inert prepared transaction is one that already ran.
8. **You review, then you sign once.**

What you do type: the human decisions. Name, symbol, supply, artwork cap, launch method, launch
protection, burn policy, quote asset, earnings mode, payout recipient. The bundle pre-populates
those and you can change them.

What you never type: a hash, a salt, a predicted address, or a byte of art configuration. Those are
derived from the bundle and from the chain, and the point of that split is that the frontend
reconstructs the same project you validated locally rather than asking you to transcribe it.

Four things a bundle deliberately does **not** carry into a draft, because importing them would be
choosing on your behalf: the chain, the quote asset, an enforced-earnings election, and any
acknowledgement you have to give.

## Step 1 — Draft

`/create` opens an implicit default draft. `/studio/<draftId>` opens a named one, and you can fork
the current work into a new named draft at any time. Drafts live in your browser's local storage,
so they are per-device and per-browser: nothing is uploaded, and nothing is recoverable if you
clear site data.

A toggle in the status bar switches between **Simple** and **Advanced**, and it only ever moves
when you click it — no validation error, chain choice, or field value silently promotes you.

Simple mode shows: name, symbol, description, template-or-code, image/logo, website, X handle,
total supply, artwork-backing units, starting-price preset, chain, and collaborator splits.
Advanced adds the exact seed field and seed history, the full sandbox, the market-to-art builder,
trait dimensions, a bps-to-percent readout, exact curve geometry, the raw metadata JSON tabs, the
license field, and a technical appendix to the governance disclosure.

Two things stay visible in Simple mode on purpose: the market-state simulation panel and the fee
disclosure, because they are comprehension and safety information rather than complexity. And
predicted contract addresses stay visible in both modes, because "read every field before you
sign" is treated as everyone's right, not a power-user feature.

## Step 2 — ART

Pick a template or write code. In Simple mode custom code is a compact text area; Advanced adds
seed controls and a link to the full sandbox at `/studio/<draftId>/sandbox`.

Always visible on this tab: a **script byte meter** showing your script size against the chain's
maximum and hard ceiling, and a market-state panel labeled SIMULATION.

The sandbox gives you a larger canvas, manual/random/sequential seeds, a saved-seed list, PNG
export, a contact sheet of up to 100 thumbnails with exact-seed duplicate detection, eleven labeled
market-simulation presets (genesis, first buys, accumulation, volatility, drawdown, recovery, thick
and thin liquidity, quiet, holder growth, fee conversion), and preview frames at app-icon,
marketplace-square, marketplace-card and social-card sizes.

Remember what [03](03-art-runtimes.md) says about the preview: it is a shared deterministic preview
renderer, not the on-chain renderer, and the market presets are simulated, not read. Use it for
composition and byte budget, not as proof.

## Step 3 — COLLECTION

Name, symbol, description, website, X handle. Total supply and artwork-backing units, with a
backing model of full parity (one token per artwork) or partial. Your creator recipient, prefilled
from the connected wallet. Collaborator fee splits — address plus bps of **your 75%**, summed live,
warned past 10,000 bps, capped at 16 on chain. Separately, attribution collaborators with roles,
which are metadata credits and carry no money. License, in Advanced, defaulting to CC0-1.0.

### Collection media

Two options: **generate from your artwork** (the default) or **upload custom media**.

Uploads go through a signed session and a one-time, scoped authorization, then a server pipeline
that sniffs the real file type, rejects anything animated or carrying an embedded second format,
normalizes to PNG at the exact role dimensions, pins to IPFS, then **fetches the asset back by its
CID and re-hashes it** before calling it verified. The status ladder you will watch is
`GENERATING → NORMALIZING → PINNING TO IPFS → VERIFYING → READY`, and a launch is blocked until it
reaches READY. See [04 — Constraints](04-constraints.md) for the exact media rules.

If you do not upload anything, a cover is generated deterministically from your own project
configuration — square, banner and featured — at a labeled neutral genesis state, and it must be
displayed with the label "Automatically generated collection cover". It is derived from
`keccak256(projectConfigHash, chainId, domain tag)`, so it is reproducible, chain-separated, and
never another project's art or a generic placeholder. Change your project config and the cover
goes stale and must be regenerated and repinned.

## Step 4 — MARKET

Choose a **starting-price tier** — LOW, MID or HIGH — which is the only raw pricing input you
supply. Everything else (tick, opening price, range, liquidity, token amounts) is computed by the
factory. In Advanced you can see the exact tick magnitudes behind each tier: HIGH is the highest
starting price, LOW the lowest.

Choose a **launch method**. The studio offers the ones a creator may actually select:

<!-- generated:launch-modes -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

| Launch method | Enum | Offered to creators | What it does |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Instant V4 (`INSTANT_V4`) | 0 | **yes** | The whole supply enters the canonical Uniswap v4 pool in one transaction. The market exists from the launch receipt. |
| Fixed-price sale (`FIXED_PRICE_SALE_TO_V4`) | 1 | **no** — `DISABLED_FOR_PUBLIC_LAUNCH` | Withdrawn. Not offered, not selectable, and refused by the contract for every caller including the protocol Safe. |
| Bonding curve (`BONDING_CURVE_SALE_TO_V4`) | 2 | **yes** | A sale along a published, versioned price curve, then a permissionless finalization that opens the canonical v4 pool. Two shipped presets: linear and constant-product. |

**Why `FIXED_PRICE_SALE_TO_V4` is not offered.** The fixed-price sale phase does not limit how much of a sale any one buyer can take: there is no per-buyer cap, no cooldown and no maximum per transaction, so a single address can acquire the entire allocation in one transaction at the moment the sale opens. The launch-protection schedule cannot apply there, because it governs the Uniswap v4 pool and that pool does not exist until the sale finalizes.

<!-- /generated:launch-modes -->

The withdrawn mode's card is not rendered at all — not greyed out, and deliberately not labelled
"coming soon". A coming-soon badge would say the mode is unfinished, when what was actually found is
a present-tense fact about what its sale phase does not do. A draft that already names it keeps its
value, shows the reason, and refuses to launch until you pick an offered method.

Bonding-curve mode adds a sale allocation, a curve preset (linear or constant-product), a duration,
a minimum raise, and optional price/target overrides.

Beside the launch method, and on a separate axis from it, you elect **launch protection** — once,
permanently. Protected is the default and choosing no protection takes an explicit acknowledgement.
[12 — Launch protection](12-launch-protection.md) is the whole of that decision; read it before you
make it, because nothing afterwards can change it.

Non-editable and displayed here: the fee split, and the fact that the project funds no quote asset
of its own into the pool.

## Step 5 — LAUNCH: review, preflight, one signature

This tab does the work, in order, against the server:

1. **Prepare** — validates your input and builds the single canonical `LaunchParams`. If the chain
   is deferred, or public launch access is still closed, the response says that directly rather
   than fabricating salts or addresses.
2. **Predict** — returns the token, collection, hook and pool id your parameters will produce.
3. **Mine the hook salt** — searches, server-side, for a salt whose resulting address carries the
   hook permission mask. A failed mine is a failed prepare; there is no zero-salt fallthrough and no
   placeholder that reaches a signature.
4. **Preflight** — a 15-point checklist. Eleven checks run server-side: chain identity, gas
   balance, predicted addresses, hook salt, pool key, recomputed gas, re-simulation, script size,
   factory codehash, external addresses, treasury. Four run locally in your browser, including the
   last one before signing: **your wallet is on the target chain right now**.
5. **Simulate** — a real `eth_call` dry run of the launch.
6. **Build** — re-simulates, then hands back an inert prepared transaction. The server never signs.
7. **You sign.** The button names the chain explicitly — "LAUNCH ON BASE", not a generic "Launch".

Also on this tab: a metadata preview (marketplace card, project page, social card in Simple;
raw ERC-7572 JSON, JSON-LD and explorer packets in Advanced) and a plain-language governance and
fee disclosure that is always visible in both modes.

On BNB Smart Chain, preflight stops before ordinary creator launch, because RC6 is not deployed
there. On Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain it does not: all three factories read `PUBLIC`. Where
preflight does refuse, it is honest about which condition it hit rather than fabricating salts or
addresses.

## Step 6 — After the launch

- Your pool is live and tradeable at the end of the launch transaction (or at graduation, in a sale
  mode).
- Holders call `awaken(count)` themselves to mint artworks against escrowed backing tokens. A buy
  materializes nothing on its own — see [02](02-what-a-launch-produces.md).
- Fees accrue in the selected quote asset and in your project token. Anyone may call `realizeFees`
  and `claimCreator`; the destination is resolved from your `ProjectRights`, so a stranger
  triggering a claim only ever pays you. See [06 — Fees and revenue](06-fees-and-revenue.md).
- **There is no second transaction.** Your collection already answers `contractURI()`, your earnings
  election is already settled, and your launch protection is already bound, in the receipt state of
  the transaction you signed. See [13 — Collection metadata](13-metadata-and-contracturi.md).
- Project and token pages live at `/p/<chainSlug>/<projectId>` and
  `/p/<chainSlug>/<projectId>/<tokenId>`; creator revenue at `/dashboard/fees`; a chain-filtered
  index at `/discover`.

## What you cannot change afterwards

The chain, the art bytes, the art mode, the market mapping, the supply, the backing ratio, the fee
split, the collaborator shares, the quote asset, the burn policy, your launch-protection election
and your creator payout-asset mode. You can change your payout recipient and your profile links, and
transferring your `ProjectRights` transfers the project including its unclaimed and future revenue.
That is the whole list — see [04 — Constraints](04-constraints.md).
